title: Wychodząc z pracy…
focus: reporting an incident: impersonal -no forms, the passive, -ąc participles, reported speech

patterns.reported: Reported speech keeps the original tense
patterns.speaker: Gender follows the speaker

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Marek, słyszałam|slyszalam, że ukradziono|ukradziono ci|ci rower|rower!
lines.en: Marek, I heard your bike was stolen!

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Tak, w piątek. Wychodząc|wychodzac z pracy, zobaczyłem|zobaczylem, że stojak jest|jest pusty.
lines.en: Yes, on Friday. As I was leaving work, I saw that the bike rack was empty.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.en: Did you report it to the police?

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Oczywiście. Policjant powiedział|powiedzial, że takich|takich kradzieży|kradziezy jest|jest2 teraz bardzo dużo.
lines.en: Of course. The officer said there are a lot of thefts like that at the moment.

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Ale wczoraj rano zadzwonił|zadzwonil do mnie sąsiad. Mój rower został|zostal znaleziony|znaleziony dwie ulice dalej!
lines.en: But yesterday morning my neighbour called me. My bike had been found two streets away!

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.en: No way! Who left it there?

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Pewnie złodziej się przestraszył|przestraszyl. Albo uznał|uznal, że rower jest za stary|stary, żeby go sprzedać.
lines.en: The thief probably got scared. Or decided the bike was too old to sell.

lines.speaker: Tomek
lines.pl: Czyli w sumie dobrze, że jeździsz|jezdzisz takim|takim gratem|gratem.
lines.en: So it’s a good thing you ride such an old wreck.

lines.speaker: Marek
lines.pl: Dzięki. Tak to sobie będę tłumaczył|tlumaczyl.
lines.en: Thanks. That’s what I’ll keep telling myself.

slyszalam.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person singular · feminine
slyszalam.why: Słyszałam, że…, “I heard that…”, the usual way to pass on news.

parts: stem of kraść (d → dź, spelled dzi)
ukradziono.why: The -no/-to form is an impersonal past: ukradziono, “someone stole, it was stolen.” It has no subject and never changes. It’s common in news and reports when nobody knows who did it.
ukradziono.compare: Other examples: znaleziono, “was found”; zbudowano, “was built”; zamknięto, “was closed.”

ci.why: The person affected goes in the dative: ukradziono ci rower, literally “the bike was stolen on you.” Polish often uses this dative where English says “your.”

rower.tags: noun · masculine inanimate · accusative singular (same as nominative)
rower.why: The -no form keeps an accusative object, as an active verb would: ukradziono rower, ukradziono torbę.
rower.history: From the English bicycle brand Rover.

wychodzac.why: The -ąc participle means “while doing.” It’s formed from the 3rd person plural present (wychodzą → wychodząc) and must share its subject with the main verb: wychodząc…, zobaczyłem, “as I was leaving, I saw.”

zobaczylem.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · masculine
zobaczylem.why: Perfective: the moment of noticing. Its imperfective partner, widzieć, is the ongoing state of seeing.

jest.why: Polish keeps the tense of the original perception or statement: zobaczyłem, że stojak jest pusty, literally “I saw that the rack is empty.” English shifts to “was.”

zglosiles.tags: verb · perfective · past · 2nd person singular · masculine
zglosiles.why: Zgłosić coś na policję, “to report something to the police.” Masculine, addressed to Marek.

policje.why: Na + accusative for where you go to report something: na policję. Being there: na policji.

powiedzial.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
powiedzial.why: Perfective: one statement. Like chcieć, it has a before ł and e before l: powiedział, but powiedzieli.

takich.why: Dużo takes the genitive plural, and the adjective agrees with its noun: takich kradzieży.

kradziezy.why: Kradzież is a feminine noun ending in a consonant; its genitive plural is -y. It comes from kraść, “to steal.”

jest2.why: Two points. Reported speech keeps the original tense: the officer said “jest dużo kradzieży.” And with dużo as the subject, the verb is third person singular: jest dużo kradzieży, “there are a lot of thefts.”

zadzwonil.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
zadzwonil.why: Zadzwonić do kogoś, “to call someone”: do + genitive, hence do mnie.

zostal.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
zostal.why: Zostać + passive participle forms the passive of perfective verbs: został znaleziony, “was found.” With imperfective verbs the auxiliary is usually być: rower był poszukiwany przez policję.

parts: stem of znaleźć (ź spelled zi before a vowel)
znaleziony.why: A passive participle agrees with its subject like an adjective: rower został znaleziony, but torba została znaleziona.

zostawil.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
zostawil.why: Kto, “who”, takes a masculine singular verb, even when nobody knows who it was.

przestraszyl.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
przestraszyl.why: Perfective: a sudden change of state. Without się, przestraszyć means “to frighten someone.”

uznal.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
uznal.why: Uznać, że…, “to decide that…”. The reported thought again keeps the present: uznał, że rower jest za stary.

stary.why: Za + adjective means “too”: za stary, “too old”; za drogi, “too expensive.” It’s often followed by żeby + infinitive: za stary, żeby go sprzedać, “too old to sell.”

jezdzisz.tags: verb · imperfective · indeterminate · present · 2nd person singular
jezdzisz.why: Jeździć is the indeterminate verb of travel by vehicle: habitual or repeated. Jechać is one trip, in one direction.

takim.why: Agrees with gratem in the instrumental.

gratem.why: Jeździć + instrumental for the vehicle: jeździć rowerem, jeździć takim gratem. Na rowerze is equally common for bikes.

tlumaczyl.tags: verb · imperfective · l-participle · masculine (future with będę)
tlumaczyl.why: Będę + l-participle: the imperfective future. Tłumaczyć sobie, “to tell oneself”; tłumaczyć also means “to translate.”

exercises.prompt: “My keys were found” (impersonal, from znaleźć): ___ moje klucze.
exercises.explain: The impersonal -no form: Znalezi + ono, “someone found / were found.”

exercises.prompt: “My bag was found” (torba): Moja torba została ___.
exercises.explain: The participle agrees with torba, so feminine -a: znalezi + on + a.
exercises.hint: Rower został znaleziony. What changes for a feminine noun?

exercises.prompt: “While reading, I fell asleep” (czytać, 3rd pl. czytają): ___, zasnąłem.
exercises.explain: The -ąc participle is built on the 3rd person plural present: czytają → Czyta + jąc.

exercises.prompt: Her words were “Jestem zmęczona.” Report them: Powiedziała, że ___ zmęczona.
exercises.explain: Polish keeps the tense of the original statement: powiedziała, że jest zmęczona.
Jeździć + instrumental for the vehicle: rowerem. Jeżdżę na rowerze is equally common.
